sourceLine: your own patent research and the questions R&D and corporate VC buyers ask before they commit

cards.title: Silicon Photonics Patents: TSMC Up, Intel Down
cards.angle: TSMC says its COUPE photonics platform enters volume production in 2026, per TrendForce (April 1, 2026). The filings showed the split a year earlier, though a few dozen filings a year is a small sample and counts alone do not measure quality.
cards.evidence: Your IP Insight #3 with TechSoda found TSMC's silicon photonics filings rose from about 46 in 2023 to about 50 in 2024, while Intel's fell from about 43 to about 26. The analysis lives on TechSoda. No page on your own site hosts it.
cards.formatNote: It rests on your own published patent counts, your strongest analytical proof.

cards.title: LLM vs Tech Scouting Platform: Which Holds Up?
cards.angle: Only 12% of organizations call their AI governance mature, per Cisco's January 2026 benchmark of 5,200 professionals. A general model is fine for brainstorming. A build or buy decision needs live sources, data that stays in-house, and a structured output, and no tool removes the need to check sources.
cards.evidence: Your homepage compares a typical LLM with Deeli on five points: sources, where prompts go, output format, workflow, and language coverage. No page on your site expands that table for buyers searching this question.
cards.formatNote: It answers the first objection a buyer raises and builds on a table you already publish.

cards.title: Chinese Patent Data: The Blind Spot in R&D
cards.angle: China filed 73,718 international patent applications in 2025, up 5.3%, and Huawei led all applicants with 7,523, per WIPO. English-only searches miss part of that signal, though machine-read technical Chinese still needs expert review on high-stakes calls.
cards.evidence: Your homepage says Deeli reads Chinese-language patents, papers, funding and disclosures. Your comparison table sets that against "English-centric general web" tools. No article on your site explains why this coverage matters.
cards.formatNote: It argues for your clearest point of difference and can rank for "Chinese patent search for R&D".
